capitals.name: Pagan (Bagan)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Pagan (849-1287)'. The rump kingdom of Kyawswa (1289-1297) still sat at Pagan; the Myinsaing brothers overthrew him there on 17 December 1297. Walls date to c. 980 at the earliest and the body adjusts the chronicle's 849 founding to 876.

keyframe_review.note: 5,368 km2 around Bagan. Infobox 'Founding of kingdom: 23 December 849'; the body says the 849 date is the chronicle's, adjusts it to 876 ('likely the founding date, not the fortification date') and notes the walls date to c. 980 at the earliest. Cliopatria starts in 850; the Pyu dossier records the founding as 849 December, so the start follows the infobox.

26,789 km2 for 860-959: the principality grows five-fold. No page opened dates a step in 860 (the page lists Pyinbya and the later kings with chronicle dates that differ by decades, 'Expansion details: page silent'); kept as Cliopatria's staging.

44,586 km2 for 960-1045 against the size the pages give for Anawrahta's principality in 1044: about 320 km north to south and 130 km east to west (about 41,600 km2) on the Pagan page, 'barely 200 miles north to south and about 80 miles from east to west' on the Anawrahta page. Ratio 1.07: the shape agrees. Dated 960-1044 because the Pyu remainder joins from 1045.

122,647 km2: the 960 principality plus 272 cells, 265 of them the Pyu remainder of Cliopatria's 1040 Pyu shape (Sri Ksetra, the Mu valley around Halin). The Pagan page lists the Pyu city-states as predecessors and says only that Anawrahta came to power in December 1044 and by the mid-1050s had made Pagan a regional power; it does not date the absorption of the Pyu cities. Dated from 1045 to match the Pyu dossier (drawn through 1044).

273,135 km2: 504 cells added, 212 of them Lower Burma (Thaton, Pegu, the delta and Yangon) and the rest the Shan Hills and the Kachin and Sagaing uplands. 'on 17 May 1057 ... the Pagan forces conquered the city' of Thaton, so the shape is dated from 1057 instead of 1056. The Shan Hills (page paraphrased): a first visit in the early to mid-1050s with tribute received, a second wave in the late 1050s and early 1060s, the 43 forts ordered on 7 February 1061.

minus.text: Arakan (Rakhine), the north reached by Anawrahta

keyframe_review.note: 439,460 km2 for 1066-1187. 593 cells added: Chin Hills, the Chindwin side of Sagaing, Kayin, Tanintharyi (the Tenasserim coast), Mon and the northern half of Rakhine. The Pagan page: Anawrahta's conquests went 'down to the Tenasserim coast, Phuket, and North Arakan', undated, and 'most scholars credit control of Arakan to Alaungsithu'; the Anawrahta page: Arakan authority is nominal (Lieberman and Charney). So Rakhine is taken out of the direct shape and drawn as a tributary (ledger vassal_start 1066, vassal_end 1287). Tenasserim: a Pali inscription at Mergui 'shows Tenasserim then paid allegiance to Pagan' (Alaungsithu page, undated). The page gives no kingdom-wide area; Western historians 'argue for a smaller empire of the Irrawaddy valley and nearer periphery' than the chronicles' present-day Myanmar and northern Thailand, and this shape is the larger reading: unverified at its edges.

minus.text: Arakan (Rakhine), the north reached by Anawrahta

keyframe_review.note: 439,571 km2, the same outline as 1066 (111 km2 more). Narapatisithu's reign 1174-1211 is the peak: 'Pagan's influence reached the Strait of Malacca, the Salween River in the east, and areas below the current China border in the north' (Pagan page); the chronicles' claims to Kengtung and Chiang Mai are not drawn. Alaungsithu's page adds that he 'reportedly sailed as far south as Malaya and Bengal' (undated). Cis-Salween Shan Hills are attributed to Narapatisithu, but they are already inside this outline; the frontier east of the Salween and the Khmer frontier (Khmer Empire from 1188, Haripunjaya) are unverified. Rakhine removed as in 1066; dated 1188-1283.

region.text: Pagan (Bagan) and its surroundings on the Irrawaddy

ledger.note: 849: Pyinbya founds Pagan on the Irrawaddy. Infobox 'Founding of kingdom: 23 December 849'; the body adjusts the chronicle's 849 to 876 and says the walls date to c. 980 at the earliest.

ledger.note: 860: the principality grows in Cliopatria's staging (5,400 to 26,800 km2). The page dates no step: Pyinbya's dates are chronicle dates and 'Expansion details: page silent' for the later kings.

region.text: the land Cliopatria moves from the Pyu to Pagan in 960

ledger.note: 960: the Burmans lead the dry zone in Cliopatria's staging (26,800 to 44,600 km2). The page gives Nyaung-u Sawrahan's reign as 931-964 (Hmannan), 959-992 (adjusted) or 956-1001 (Zatadawbon) and no expansion.

region.text: the Pyu land still outside Pagan in 1044: Sri Ksetra, the southern dry zone and the Mu valley around Halin

ledger.note: 1044: Anawrahta comes to power at Pagan and the Pyu remainder passes under Pagan. 'On 16 December 1044, Min Saw ascended the throne with the title of Anawrahta' (Anawrahta page; Pagan page: 'In December 1044, a Pagan prince named Anawrahta came to power'). Neither page dates the absorption of the Pyu cities; Cliopatria draws it in 1046 and the Pyu dossier in December 1044. Anawrahta's own principality in 1044 is the 960 shape ('barely 200 miles north to south').

region.text: the Shan Hills and the Kachin and Sagaing uplands, as Cliopatria adds them in 1056

ledger.note: 1057: the Shan Hills and the northern uplands come under Pagan. The page (paraphrased) has a first visit in the early to mid-1050s with tribute received, a second wave in the late 1050s and early 1060s after the Nanzhao march, and the 43 forts ordered on 7 February 1061. The year is Cliopatria's (shape 1056); the page dates no single conquest.

1057: Anawrahta conquers Thaton and Lower Burma. He 'invaded the southern kingdom in early 1057' and 'on 17 May 1057 (11th waxing of Nayon, 419 ME), the Pagan forces conquered the city'; Pegu's ruler submitted first (no date) and was kept as a vassal until his death. Aung-Thwin argues Thaton's role is a post-Pagan legend and that Lower Burma lacked a substantial polity. Cliopatria draws the shape from 1056.

region.text: Tenasserim, the Chin Hills, Kayin and Mon uplands and the Chindwin side of Sagaing

ledger.note: 1066: Pagan reaches the Tenasserim coast, the Chin Hills and the Kayin and Mon uplands. 'He began in the Shan Hills and extended conquests down to the Tenasserim coast, Phuket, and North Arakan' (undated; 'over the next decade he founded the empire'). The Anawrahta page: Khmer forces invaded Tenasserim and were repulsed, date silent. 1066 is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Arakan (Rakhine), the north reached by Anawrahta

ledger.note: 1066: North Arakan under Pagan's overlordship. Anawrahta 'reached North Arakan' (a march over the pass from Ngape to An and a siege of Pyinsa; date silent) but Lieberman and Charney doubt Pagan had 'effective authority' over Arakan, which the page treats as nominal; 'most scholars credit control of Arakan to Alaungsithu' (Pagan page), who restored the Arakanese heir in 1118 (Arakanese chronicles: 1103) on the Alaungsithu page. Cliopatria's Chandra Dynasty row (900-1055) overlaps 69 cells of this land. [Review fix fx-33, 2026-11-01: 'arakan' (the Vesali-era Arakan, 1066-1236) has no dossier; the relation is closed with it in 1237 and continues with launggyet-kingdom, see the two events dated 1237.]

ledger.note: 1237 (bridge, review fix fx-33, 2026-11-01): Arakan, now the Launggyet kingdom, is Pagan's nominal tributary. Pagan Kingdom page: Arakan is among the outlying tributary lands, "tributary lands over which the crown only had a 'largely ritual' or nominal sovereignty" (no date), "Pagan largely stayed out of the affairs of these outlying states, only interfering when there were outright revolts, such as Arakan and Martaban in the late 1250s", and "In the west too, Arakan stopped paying tribute" after 1287; Lieberman is cited as doubting any "effective authority" over Arakan. wars.name: Conquest of Thaton
wars.outcome: Anawrahta invaded the south in early 1057 and Pagan forces took Thaton on 17 May 1057; Pegu submitted and was held as a vassal; Lower Burma came under Pagan.
wars.note: Aung-Thwin argues the Thaton story is a post-Pagan legend; the page says the real aim was checking Khmer expansion.

wars.name: Khmer-Pagan clash on the Tenasserim coast

zones.text: Tenasserim coast, where victory tablets were found

wars.outcome: Khmer forces invaded Tenasserim and Anawrahta's generals repulsed them; the date is not given, so the span is the reign.
wars.note: Siamese chronicles claim Anawrahta conquered the Menam valley and sacked Angkor; the Pagan page treats it as a claim and the Khmer Empire dossier does not draw it.

wars.name: Revolts of Arakan and Martaban
wars.outcome: Revolts in Macchagiri (Arakan) and Martaban in 1256-1259 under Narathihapate; Martaban rebelled again in 1285; no change of border is recorded.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey on the pages opened fixes any Pagan frontier; the Shan Hills, Tenasserim and Arakan edges are approximate (the chronicles' claims to Chiang Mai and Kengtung are not drawn). The Mongol frontier at Tagaung (1284) is the only dated line.

notes:
Cliopatria checks. Eight shapes (850-1293) reviewed; the 1285-1293 shape is marked wrong (the full 439,571 km2 outline is kept to 1293 although the Mongols hold the north from 1284, Lower Burma goes in January 1287 and the page leaves 'only a small area around the capital' from 1289); two new keyframes (1284, 1287) replace it. The end moves from Cliopatria's 1293 to 17 December 1297 (Pagan page body and First Mongol invasion page), which overlaps the Myinsaing, Hanthawaddy and Shan States rows that start in 1294; their dossiers should start in 1287 (Hanthawaddy) or 1297 (Myinsaing), not 1294. The Pagan page's infobox gives the Myinsaing takeover as 17 December 1287 and the capital as 'Pagan (849-1287)'; its body says 1297.

Area check: the page gives no kingdom-wide area. The 1044 principality (about 320 km by 130 km on the Pagan page, about 41,600 km2) matches the 44,586 km2 shape of 960-1045 (ratio 1.07). The 439,000 km2 outline from 1066 is the larger of the two readings the Anawrahta page sets side by side (chronicles: present-day Myanmar and northern Thailand; Western historians: the Irrawaddy valley and nearer periphery). Its edges are unverified.

What the pages did not settle (conf 1): the 860 and 960 steps; when the Pyu cities passed (1044 per the Pyu dossier, 1046 on Cliopatria); the 1057 Shan Hills and 1066 Tenasserim/Chin/Kayin gains (the Pagan page says 'over the next decade'); the 1287 Shan secession and the 'rest of the kingdom' loss. Not drawn: the chronicles' claims on Chiang Mai, Kengtung and the Menam valley; Pegu added to the Khmer Empire by Chinese sources in 1195 (Khmer Empire page) which lies inside this outline; the Mongol Mianzhong deal (tentative 3 March 1286, ended 18 August 1290) and the 1300-1303 second invasion (after the end).

Arakan is drawn as a tributary (vassal_start 1066, vassal_end 1287), not as direct land: the Anawrahta page treats Pagan's authority there as nominal. The counterpart string 'arakan' has no dossier or Cliopatria row (Cliopatria's Chandra Dynasty, 900-1055, overlaps 69 cells of the same land; the Kingdom of Mrauk U starts 1429). 'mon-city-states' (Thaton and the Mon country, c. 825-1057) has none either.

Needs from others: pyu-city-states already carries the matching 849, 860, 960 and 1044 events; hanthawaddy-kingdom should start 1287 (Wareru, 30 January); yuan-dynasty should carry the 1284 gain of northern Burma (Zhengmian to 1303); myinsaing-kingdom the 1297 gain; shan-states the 1287 gain. The khmer-empire dossier has no matching event for the Tenasserim clash (date silent). Rulers omitted: the page's reign dates differ by chronicle (Hmannan vs Zatadawbon vs adjusted) until 1044.

Page budget: five pages; the Mongol invasions of Burma page was a disambiguation page and added nothing but the two war dates, so the first Mongol invasion article was opened as well. The Pagan page, the Anawrahta page and the First Mongol invasion page carry the dossier; the Alaungsithu page is thin (no extents, no dated conquests).

Gazetteer names used: 'Lower Burma' (region), 'Tenasserim' (region), Rakhine, Shan, Bagan. The polygon for 'northern Burma to Tagaung' (a 12-point fallback, 4 points) has no named region; the gazetteer agent could add 'Zhengmian' or 'Upper Burma north of Tagaung'.
